name: COMET TRAIL
blurb: A white-hot gold comet head rides the cursor, streaming a tapered lime-to-pink spark tail that stretches with speed and settles into a pulsing ember with orbiting glints when you stop.
issues: Minor (not a violation): before the first pointer move nothing renders, but contract only requires visibility within 2s of moving — idle-after-move has pulsing glow, orbiting sparks, and embers
Minor (not a violation): fillStyle strings are rebuilt in the particle loop (~260/frame); unavoidable with continuously varying alpha and within 60fps budget since no shadowBlur is used
Note: one createRadialGradient allocation per frame for the head glow — single allocation outside hot loops, acceptable

name: CONSTELLATION WAKE
blurb: Twinkling stars drop along your path and wire themselves into a glowing constellation that draws itself in and fades; clicking stamps a ringed asterism.

name: WARP FIELD
blurb: Cyan-white star streaks smear backward from the cursor and accelerate away, stretching with your speed like punching into warp.

name: ORBIT SWARM
blurb: Nine tiny moons on tilted Kepler ellipses lag elastically behind your cursor, tightening into a gyroscopic atom at rest — click to shock-reverse their orbits.
issues: Verified by execution in Node with mocked env: parses as a single function expression and returns {move, frame, down}.
frame() begins with env.fade(0.28) — clearing rule satisfied (confirmed first ctx-level op at runtime).
No window/document/DOM/timer/rAF usage (static scan clean); sizes only via env.W()/H() at init.
Pools strictly bounded: 9 moons + 4 reused shock slots; 5000 rapid down() calls caused no growth.
Colors all palette-derived rgba, raw palette hexes, or white — compliant.
Numerically stable: no NaN/Infinity passed to ctx across 600 frames with dt=0, 500ms dt spikes (dt capped at 50ms), fast random moves, clicks, and a 0x0 canvas.
Performance: ~47 draw ops/frame (plain arcs/ellipses), zero shadowBlur, no per-frame allocations in hot loops — within budget.

Idle look confirmed: moons keep orbiting at tightened radius (baseline mul 0.45 plus breathing sine), rings visible; 'tighten when still / lag when moving' brief implemented via per-moon springs and energy-scaled radii.
Minor non-blocking: t and m.ang grow unbounded (negligible double-precision drift, only after hours); down() reverses all orbit directions per click — reads as intentional design, not a defect.

name: PIXEL STARDUST
blurb: Chunky 8-bit pixels burst off the cursor, tumble under gravity, and strobe out like tiny arcade fireworks.

name: PLASMA RIBBON
blurb: A silky spring-chased neon ribbon that shimmers cyan-to-pink along its tapered length, coils lazily when idle, and flares with a shockwave on click.
issues: Informational: dt values >= 40ms are clamped to 16.7ms, so on sub-25fps machines the ribbon runs slightly slow-motion instead of time-compensating (stability tradeoff, not a contract violation).

Informational: 189 two-point strokes per frame (63 segments x 3 glow passes) is stroke-heavy but uses no shadowBlur and no per-frame gradient/string allocation; verified within 60fps budget expectations.

Verified in a mock-env harness: fade-first every frame, fixed pools (64 points + 3 shocks), all 126 emitted colors on the cyan-to-pink ramp or its whitened core, 0 non-finite coords over 8M drawn across 10k idle frames, erratic fast moves, and hostile dt (0, -5, NaN, 5000); down() before any move/frame and zero-size canvas both safe; state reset to source-over/alpha 1 at frame end.

name: ROCKET THRUSTER
blurb: A cyan rocket nozzle rides your cursor, blasting a gold-core, pink-edged flame cone with mach diamonds opposite your motion, settling to a flickering pilot light when you stop.
issues: frame() did not literally begin with a clear: a dt clamp (`if (dt > 40) dt = 40;`) preceded env.fade(0.3). Harmless at runtime, but violates a strict reading of the 'MUST begin by clearing' rule — moved env.fade(0.3) to the first statement (fade is dt-independent, so behavior is identical).
Minor, not fixed (harmless): `t` and `emit` accumulate unboundedly as doubles — precision loss would only matter after days of continuous runtime.

Verified OK: bounded 400-particle pool with circular reuse; no DOM/window/timer usage; all colours are palette-derived (gold->pink LUT, white, cyan) — validated per-channel via a mock ctx; returns {move, frame, down}; idle state draws pilot-light flicker + glow + cyan nozzle every frame; no shadowBlur; only one gradient allocation per frame, particle loop allocation-free; survives dt=0, dt=5000 (clamped), zero-delta moves, and click bursts without NaN reaching draw calls.

name: GRAVITY LENS
blurb: A dim starfield leans into your cursor's gravity well, brightening and swirling as space bends — click to collapse the lens.
issues: No contract violations found. Verified by executing the module in Node with an instrumented ctx: env.clear() is always the first canvas op in frame(); all fill/stroke colours are palette-derived rgba (zero violations over ~7500 frames); pool bounded to 80-300 stars rebuilt only on resize; hot loop is allocation-free via a precomputed colour LUT (indices verified in bounds); NaN/0/undefined dt guarded and clamped; 5000-frame stress with clicks, resizes, and degenerate cursor positions produced zero non-finite draw-call arguments; idle renders a dim twinkling starfield.

Minor, non-blocking: up to 3 small alpha strings allocated per frame for the ring/pulse strokes (outside the star loop); `time` accumulator grows unbounded (sin precision only degrades after days of uptime); negative dt is unguarded but rAF never delivers it.

name: STATIC CRACKLE
blurb: Fast flicks throw jagged cyan-white static arcs off the cursor; slow moves settle into a calm charged glow.
issues: No contract violations found. Minor notes only: rgba strings are rebuilt via toFixed for live elements each frame (bounded by pool size, acceptable); one createRadialGradient allocation per frame for the cursor glow (within 60fps budget); before the first pointer event the canvas stays blank, which is graceful since the cursor position is unknown.

name: EVENT HORIZON
blurb: A miniature black hole rides your cursor — debris spirals down decaying orbits and flares out on a pink-gold accretion ring.
issues: FIXED: frame() ran two bookkeeping statements (dt clamp, time accumulation) before env.fade(0.28); the contract says frame MUST begin by clearing, so env.fade(0.28) was moved to the very first statement (it does not depend on dt).

FIXED: the dark-disc gradient's outer stop used 'rgba(6,6,9,0)' — the page background colour, which is not a palette colour, white, or black. Replaced with the visually identical fully-transparent 'rgba(0,0,0,0)'.

VERIFIED OK (no change): pools are hard-capped and preallocated — 380 particles (<=400), 28 impact flashes, 5 click shockwaves — all reused via alive flags; spawn() silently drops when full. Particle radius decays strictly monotonically toward the ring, so every particle dies and recycles; confirmed under a 3000-event spawn-storm test.

VERIFIED OK (no change): frame budget — no shadowBlur anywhere; at most 31 gradients/frame (3 for disc/ring + <=28 short-lived flashes) and 35 arcs/frame; trail strokes are plain 1-segment lines. Only per-frame allocations are bounded gradient objects and rgba colour strings (the dynamic pink->gold->white trail colour cannot be a static literal).

VERIFIED OK (no change): idle behaviour — before any pointer event, frame() self-centres the horizon at W/2,H/2 and an idle spawner emits an orbiting particle every ~260 ms, so the ring plus occasional infall is visible with the cursor still; a 60 s idle drain ran clean.

VERIFIED OK (no change): dt is clamped to [0.1, 34] ms, so dt=0, undefined, negative, and huge tab-restore spikes cannot explode the simulation (all four cases exercised in the smoke test); trail segments longer than 40 px are skipped, preventing ugly streaks when the lerped centre jumps.

VERIFIED OK (no change): no window/document/DOM/timer/rAF usage; sizes only via env.W()/env.H(); colours only palette pink/gold (255,46,163 / 255,222,46), white, black, and interpolations between them; returns {move, frame, down} with move and frame present; gradient colour stops are in ascending order; composite mode and globalAlpha are reset to source-over/1 at frame end so env.fade works next frame.
